title: Federal and unitary countries
examples: What is the difference between federal and unitary?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Both share work; who has the final say differs

explain.say: Think of a big family. In some, the parents decide almost everything. In others, each grown child runs their own house but follows a few family rules. Countries are the same. Look at the board: federal countries on the left, unitary ones on the right.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Both share work; who has the final say differs

explain.say: See the federal side? Federal means power is shared between a central government and states or provinces, and the constitution protects each share. The USA, India, Brazil, Nigeria, Germany and Australia are federal. Do you live in a state or province?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Both share work; who has the final say differs

explain.say: Now the unitary side. Unitary means the central government holds top power; it can give jobs to regions or take them back. France, Japan, China, Indonesia and Egypt are unitary. Can you spot the key difference? It is who has the final say.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Both share work; who has the final say differs

explain.say: Here is a real example. India's constitution sorts jobs into three lists: defence and money for the Union, police and farming for the states, and education shared by both. Quick check: which list would trains go in? The Union list!

explain.say: Federal systems suit huge, varied countries; unitary systems can act fast and keep rules the same everywhere. Super thinking! Wow: the UK is unitary, yet it has devolved, which means handed down, many powers to Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

faq.a: In a federal country, power is shared by law between a national government and regional governments, like states or provinces. Neither can simply take away the other's powers.
In a unitary country, the central government holds top power. It may give regions or cities some jobs, but it can change or take back those powers.
Devolution means a central government hands some powers down to regions, like the UK giving Scotland its own parliament in 1999. The centre could, in law, take them back.

faq.q: Why are big countries often federal?
faq.a: Large or varied countries like India, Brazil, Nigeria and the USA have many regions, languages and needs. A federal system lets each state make some choices while staying one country.

faq.q: Which jobs belong to the central government?
faq.a: Usually defence, foreign affairs, currency and borders. In India these are on the Union list, along with railways.
asks: What does the national government control?

facts: India's constitution divides powers into a Union list, a State list and a Concurrent list.
About 25 countries, home to around 40 percent of the world's people, have federal systems.
